Hi Samir / Laura — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can keep your security team unblocked: 

- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in 2025; I can share a redacted report and a drive link for your security review.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We support GDPR contractual controls; for HIPAA we can execute a BAA (attached is our standard BAA template).
- Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor list (PDF) and a short inventory of cloud providers and regions.
- Vendor questionnaire: Ill send a link to our vendor security questionnaire (we also accept your XLSX if you prefer).

Requested from Acme: please confirm whether you have any specific data residency or encryption key requirements (customer-managed keys, required region). Also confirm the scope (whether PHI will be processed) so we can route to legal/security as needed.

Next steps:
1) Ill attach the SOC 2 redacted report + subprocessors + questionnaire link (below).
2) Please share any completed vendor questionnaire or specific asks by EOW.
3) If there’s a technical security check, Dylan (cc’d) can join a call with your infra/security team next week.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20261026.pdf, redwood_soc2_report_redacted_20251001.pdf, Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf

Hi Marissa — appreciated the call. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

- Can you confirm SOC 2 Type (Type II?) and the date it was issued? We usually request the latest Type II report or a bridge letter.
- Which cloud providers and regions will store/process our data? We have EU residency requirements for a portion of the dataset.
- For HIPAA: do you sign BAAs and do your subprocessors have access to plaintext PHI?

Happy to fill out the attached XLSX but if you can provide links/docs that’s faster. If possible, could Dylan join for a short tech call next Wed (10/28) 10-11am PT?

Hi Samir — quick answers inline and resources attached.

- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2025-09-30; redacted report attached (redwood_soc2_report_redacted_20251001.pdf) and a link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/shared/redwood_soc2_redacted.pdf. If you need a bridge letter, we can request one from our external auditor — let us know.

- Cloud providers / regions: Primary compute and storage are on AWS (us-west-2) and GCP (us-central1) for redundancy; we can restrict EU workloads to GCP/eu-west-1 upon request. See attached subprocessors PDF for full list (includes RedisLabs, Sentry, Segment for telemetry, etc.).

- HIPAA / BAA: We do sign BAAs. Our standard BAA template is attached (Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf). Subprocessors access: subprocessors that process customer content do so under contract and are subject to our data processing addendum; access to plaintext PHI is restricted — we can provide a short statement of subprocessor access controls and encryption practices.

- Encryption & KMS: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we use AES-256. We offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers can request CMEK in certain enterprise plans — if that’s a hard requirement we can scope it in the deal.

Next step: Dylan, can you propose 30-minute slots on Wed (10/28) 10-11am PT or Thu (10/29) 9-11am PT to go over any infra-level checks? Samir / Laura, once you review the attachments you can either confirm via email or add comments to the vendor questionnaire form: https://forms.redwood.example.com/vendor-questionnaire/ACME-8921

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Security info & subprocessor list

Thanks Marissa. A few items from legal/security review after a quick look at the attachments: 

1) We need confirmation whether any Redwood subprocessors have the ability to access plaintext customer content in the hosted offering (not dedicated). If yes, we need a list of roles and controls.
2) For GDPR: please confirm data transfer mechanisms (SCCs in place?) and whether Redwood will accept our DPA redlines for standard clauses (we will circulate redlines if we proceed).
3) For HIPAA: good to see BAA template — can you confirm turnaround for signed BAA (we typically expect < 10 business days once both counsels are aligned).

Also, can you confirm whether you maintain an inventory of subprocessors with last-sync dates? We prefer to see a timestamp on the subprocessors list.

If you could provide short written answers to 1–3 above before the call, that would help our side.

Laura Chen
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
laura.chen@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Security info & subprocessor list

Dylan / Lauren — FYI I’m sending the answers Laura requested and attaching the subprocessors PDF with a last-updated timestamp (2026-10-26). Please see the draft responses below which I'll send to Acme in the next 30–45 mins (feel free to edit):

- Plaintext access: For hosted customers, a small set of subprocessors (e.g., S3 logs processing, monitoring providers) may process customer content in controlled environments. Access is restricted by role-based access controls, MFA, least privilege, and logging; subprocessors with access are bound by contract and undergo quarterly security reviews.
- Data transfers / SCCs: We execute SCCs for EU customers and maintain a DPA; we are happy to review your redlines (send them along) and typically negotiate feasible exceptions.
- BAA turnaround: Once both counsel are aligned we can sign within ~7–10 business days; for Dedicated/Private deployments timelines are often faster.

I’ll schedule the 30-min infra call for Wed 10/28 10:30am PT (Dylan please accept and include a calendar invite).

Thanks — Marissa
